body.text: Apohasiddhiḥ /
body.translated_text: <s>Apohasiddhi</s> (Establishment of Exclusion).

body.text: namaḥ śrīlokanāthāya //
body.translated_text: Homage to the glorious <s>Lokanātha</s> (Lord of the World).

body.text: apohaḥ śabdārtho nirucyate /
body.translated_text: <s>Apoha</s> (exclusion) is explained as the meaning of words.

body.text: nanu ko 'yaṃ apoho nāma? kimidaṃ anyasmādapohyate; asmādvā anyadapohyate; asmin vānyadapohyata iti vyutpattyā vijātivyāvṛttaṃ vāhya meva vivakṣitaṃ; buddhyākāro vā; yadi vā apohanaṃ apoha ityanya vyāvṛttimātraṃ iti trayaḥ pakṣāḥ / na tāvadādimau pakṣau, apohanāmnā vidhereva vivakṣitatvāt; antimo 'pyasaṅgataḥ prati tivādhitatvāt; tathāhi parvvatoddeśe vanhirastīti śābdau pratītirvvidhirūpamevollikhantī lakṣyate; nānagnirnabhavatīti nivṛttimātramāmukhayantī / yacca pratyakṣavādhitaṃ na tatra sādhanāntarāvakāśa ityatiprasiddham /
body.translated_text: Now, what indeed is this thing called <s>apoha</s>? Is it that this is excluded from another; or that another is excluded from this; or that another is excluded in this? By etymology, there are three positions: is the intended [meaning] the external [object] differentiated from heterogeneous kinds (<s>vijātivyāvṛtta</s>); or the form of cognition (<s>buddhyākāra</s>); or is <s>apoha</s> the act of excluding, namely, mere differentiation from others (<s>anyavyāvṛttimātra</s>)? The first two positions are not [correct], because under the name '<s>apoha</s>' it is the positive entity (<s>vidhi</s>) itself that is intended. The last [position] is also untenable, because it is contradicted by cognition. For indeed, in the case of 'there is fire on the mountain,' the verbal cognition is observed to delineate only a positive form, not presenting merely a negation [of the form] 'it is not non-fire.' And it is well established that where something is contradicted by perception, there is no scope for another means of proof.

body.text: atha yadyapi nivṛttimahaṃ pratyemīti na vikalpaḥ / tathāpi nivṛttapadārthollekha eva nivṛttyullekhaḥ / na hyanantarbhāvitaviśeṣaṇapratīti vviśiṣṭapratītiḥ / tato yathā sāmānyamahaṃ pratyemīti vikalpābhāve 'pi sādhāraṇākāraparisphuraṇāt vikalpabuddhiḥ sāmānyabuddhiḥ pareṣām; tathā nivṛttapratyayā kṣiptā nivṛttibuddhirapohapratītivyavahāramātanotīti cet? nanu sādhāraṇākāraparisphuraṇe vidhirūpatayā yadi sāmānyabodhavyavasthā; tat kimāyātamasphu radabhāvākāre cetasi nivṛttipratītivyavasthāyāḥ / tato nivṛttimahaṃ pratyemītyevamākārābhāve 'pi nivṛttyākārasphuraṇaṃ yadi syāt, ko nāma nivṛttipratītisthitimapalapet / anyathāsati pratibhāse tatpratītivyavahṛtiriti gavākārepi cetasi turagabodha ityastu /
body.translated_text: Now, even though there is no conceptual cognition (<s>vikalpa</s>) of the form 'I cognize a negation,' nevertheless the delineation of a negated referent is itself the delineation of negation. For there is no cognition of the qualified without the cognition of the qualifier being included within it. Therefore, just as others hold that conceptual cognition is a cognition of the universal (<s>sāmānya</s>), even in the absence of a concept 'I cognize the universal,' because of the manifestation of a common form; similarly, the cognition of negation, implied by the cognition of the negated object, extends the conventional usage of <s>apoha</s>-cognition — is that [the argument]? But if the determination of universal-cognition is due to the manifestation of the common form in a positive manner, then what basis is there for the determination of negation-cognition in a mind in which the form of absence does not manifest? Therefore, if the manifestation of the form of negation were to occur even in the absence of a cognition of the form 'I cognize negation,' who indeed would deny the existence of negation-cognition? Otherwise, if the conventional usage of cognizing that [negation] occurs without its manifestation, then let there be cognition of a horse even when the form of a cow is in the mind.

body.text: atha viśeṣaṇatayā antarbhūtā nivṛttipratītirityuktaṃ, tathāpi yadyagavāpoḍha itīdṛśā kārovikalpastadā viśeṣaṇatayā tadanupraveśo bhavatu, kintu gauriti pratītiḥ / tadā ca satopi nivṛttilakṣaṇasya viśeṣaṇasya tatrānutkalanāt; kathaṃ tat pratītivyavasthā / athaivaṃ matiḥ / yadvidhirūpaṃ sphuritaṃ tasya parāpoho 'pyastīti tatpratītirucyate / tathāpi sambandhamātramapohasya vidhireva sākṣānnirbhāsī / api caivamadhyakṣasyā pyapohaviṣayatvamanivāryam / viśeṣato vikalpādekavyāvṛttollekhino 'khilānyavyāvṛttamīkṣamāṇasya / tasmādvidhyākārāvagrahādadhyakṣavadvikalpasyāpi vidhiviṣayatvameva nānyāpohaviṣayatvamiti kathamapohaḥ śabdārtho ghuṣyate // atrābhidhīyate //
body.translated_text: Now, if it is said that the cognition of negation is included as a qualifier — even so, if the concept is of such a form as 'excluded from non-cow' (<s>agavāpoḍha</s>), then let the entry [of negation] be as a qualifier. But [we observe only] the cognition 'it is a cow.' And then, since the qualifier characterized by negation, even though present, does not manifest therein, how can the determination of that cognition [as negation-cognition] be maintained? Or if the view is this: that which manifests in positive form also possesses the exclusion of others, and so that cognition is called [<s>apoha</s>-cognition] — even so, it is only a relation of <s>apoha</s> [to the positive], and it is the positive entity (<s>vidhi</s>) alone that directly appears. Moreover, in this way it is unavoidable that perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>) too would have <s>apoha</s> as its object — especially for one who sees complete differentiation from all others on the basis of a concept that delineates only one differentiation. Therefore, since conceptual cognition grasps the positive form just as perception does, its object is the positive entity alone, not the exclusion of others — so how can <s>apoha</s> be proclaimed as the meaning of words? To this, [we] reply:

body.text: nāsmābhirapohaśabdena vidhireva kevalo 'bhipretaḥ / nāpyanyavyāvṛttimātraṃ, kintvanyāpohaviśiṣṭo vidhiḥ śabdānāmarthaḥ / tataśca na pratyekapakṣopanipātidoṣāvakāśaḥ / yattu goḥ pratītau na tadātmāparātmeti sāmarthyādapohaḥ paścānniścīyata iti vidhivādināṃ matam; anyāpohapratītau vā sāmarthyāt anyāpoḍhovadhāryyate iti pratiṣedhavādināṃ matam / tadasundaram / prāthamikasyāpi pratipattikramādarśanāt / na hi vidhiṃ pratīpadya kaścidarthāpattitaḥ paścādapohamavagacchati; apohaṃ vā pratipadyānyāpodam; tasmād goḥ pratipattiriti anyāpoḍhapratipattirucyate / yadyapi cānyāpoḍhaśabdānullekha uktaḥ / tathāpi nāpratipattireva, viśeṣaṇabhūtasyānyāpohasya agavāpoḍha eva gośabdasya niveśitatvāt / yathā nīlotpale niveśitādindīvaraśabdānnīlotpala pratītau tatkāla eva nīlimasphuraṇamanivāryyam; tathā gośabdādapyagavāpoḍhe niveśitāt gopratītau tulyakālameva viśeṣaṇatvāt ago[']pohasphuraṇamanivāryyam / yathā pratyakṣasya prasahya rūpābhāvagrahaṇamabhāvavikalpotpādana śaktireva / tathā vidhivikalpānāmapi tadanurūpānuṣṭhānadānaśaktirevābhāvagrahaṇamabhidhīyate / paryyudāsarūpābhāvagrahaṇantu niyata svarūpasambedanamubhayoraviśiṣṭaṃ; anyathā yadi śabdādarthapratipattikāle kalito na parāpohaḥ; kathamanyaparihāreṇa pravṛttiḥ / tato gāṃ vadhāneti codito 'śvādīnapi vadhnīyāt /
body.translated_text: By the word <s>apoha</s> we do not intend the positive entity (<s>vidhi</s>) alone, nor merely the exclusion of others (<s>anyavyāvṛttimātra</s>), but rather a positive entity qualified by the exclusion of others (<s>anyāpohaviśiṣṭo vidhiḥ</s>) is the meaning of words. And thus there is no scope for the defect of falling into one [member] of the pair separately. As for the view of the proponents of the positive entity (<s>vidhivādins</s>) — that in the cognition of a cow there is no [explicit thought] 'this is its own nature, that is another's nature,' and so by implication exclusion (<s>apoha</s>) is determined afterwards; or the view of the proponents of negation (<s>pratiṣedhavādins</s>) — that in the cognition of the exclusion of others, by implication that-which-is-excluded-from-others is determined — that is not sound. Because no sequence of apprehension is observed even in the case of the very first [cognition]. For no one, having apprehended the positive entity, afterwards understands the exclusion through presumption (<s>arthāpatti</s>); nor, having apprehended the exclusion, [understands] that which is excluded from others; therefore the apprehension of the cow is called the apprehension of that which is excluded from others (<s>anyāpoḍha</s>). And although it is said that there is no [explicit] reference to the word 'excluded from others,' nevertheless it is not the case that there is no apprehension at all, because the exclusion of others, which constitutes the qualifier, is lodged in the word 'cow' precisely as 'excluded from non-cow' (<s>agavāpoḍha</s>). Just as, the word '<s>indīvara</s>' (blue lotus) being lodged in [the meaning] blue lotus, in the cognition of the blue lotus the flashing-forth of blueness is at that very moment unavoidable; so too, the word 'cow' being lodged in 'excluded from non-cow,' in the cognition of the cow the flashing-forth of the exclusion of non-cow is unavoidable at the very same moment, since it is a qualifier. Just as the grasping by perception, perforce, of the absence of form is itself the power to produce the conceptual cognition of absence; so too the power of the positive conceptual cognitions to grant action conforming to that [object] is itself called the grasping of absence. But the grasping of absence in the form of exclusion-implying-affirmation (<s>paryudāsa</s>) is the awareness of a determinate own-nature, which is common to both [the positive entity and exclusion]; otherwise, if at the time of apprehending the object from a word the exclusion of others were not delineated, how could there be activity by way of avoiding the others? Then one who is enjoined 'tie up the cow' would tie up horses and the like as well.

body.text: yadapyavocadvācaspatiḥ; jātimatyo vyaktavyaḥ; vikalpānāṃ śabdānāñca gocaraḥ; tāsāñca tadvatīnāṃ rūpamatajjātīyaparāvṛttamityarthatastadavagaterna gāmbadhāneti co dito 'śvādīn badhnāti / tadapyanenaiva nirastaṃ yato jāteradhikāyāḥ prakṣepe 'pi vyaktīnāṃ rūpamatajjātīyavyāvṛttameva cet, tadā tenaiva rūpeṇa śabdavikalpayorviṣayībhavantīnāṃ kathamatadyāvṛttiparihāraḥ?
body.translated_text: And as for what <s>Vācaspati</s> said: that which possesses the universal (<s>jātimat</s>) is to be expressed; that is the scope of conceptual cognitions and of words; and the form of those things possessing the universal is excluded from what is not of that kind (<s>atajjātīyaparāvṛtta</s>) — so that, since [the object] is understood [only] through implication, one enjoined 'tie up the cow' does not tie up horses and the like — that too is refuted by this very [argument]. For even granting the superimposition of the universal (<s>jāti</s>), if the form of the individuals is indeed excluded from what is not of that kind, then since they become the object of word and conceptual cognition by that very form, how is the avoidance of [the apprehension of] non-exclusion accomplished?

body.text: atha na vijātīyavyāvṛttaṃ vyaktirūpaṃ, tathāpratītaṃ, vā tadā jātiprasāda eṣa iti kathamarthatopi tadavagatirityuktaprāyam /
body.translated_text: But if the form of the individual is not excluded from the heterogeneous kind, or is not so apprehended, then this is the gracious gift of the universal — [yet] how, even by implication, is there cognition of that [exclusion]? This has already been virtually stated.

body.text: atha jātivalādevānyato vyāvṛttam / bhavatu jātivalāt svahetuparamparāvalādvānyavyāvṛttam / ubhayathāpi vyāvṛttapratipattau vyāvṛttipratipattirastyeva / nacāgo[']poḍhe gośabdasaṅketavidhāvanyonyāśrayadoṣaḥ / sāmānye tadvati vā saṅkete 'pi taddoṣāvakāśāt / na hi sāmānyaṃ nāma sāmānyamātramabhipretam turagepi gośabdasaṅketaprasaṅgāt / kintu gotvam / tāvatā ca sa eva doṣaḥ / gavāparijñāne gotvasāmānyāparijñānāt / gotvasāmānyāparijñane gośabdavācyāparijñānāt / tasmāt ekapiṇḍadarśanapūrvvako yaḥ sarvvavyaktisādhāraṇa iva bahiradhya sto vikalpabudhyākāraḥ, tatrāyaṃ gauriti saṅketakaraṇe netaretarāśrayadoṣaḥ / abhimate ca gośabdapravṛttāvagośabdena śeṣasyāpyabhidhāna mucitam / na cānyāpoḍhā nyāpohayorvvirodhoviśeṣyaviśeṣaṇakṣatirvvā; parasparavyavacchedābhāvāt, sāmānādhikaraṇyasadbhāvāt, bhūtalaghaṭābhāvavat / svābhāvena hi virodho na parābhāvenetyābālaprasiddhaṃ / eṣa panthāḥ śrughnamupatiṣṭhata ityatrāpyapoho gamyata eva; aprakṛta pathāntarāpekṣayā eṣa eva / śrughnapratyanīkāniṣṭasthānāpekṣayā śrughnameva / araṇyamārgavadvicchedābhāvādupatiṣṭhata eva / sārthadūtādivyavacchedena panthāeveti pratipadaṃ vyavacchedasya sulabhatvāt tasmādapohadharmmaṇo vidhirūpasya śabdādavagatiḥ; puṇḍarīkaśabdādiva śvetimaviśiṣṭasya padmasya / yadyevaṃ vidhireva śabdārthovaktumucitaḥ / kathamapoho gīyata iti cet? uktamatrāpohaśabdenānyāpohaviśiṣṭo vidhirucyate; tatra vidhau pratīyamāne viśeṣaṇatayā tulyakālamanyāpohapratītiriti / na caivaṃ pratyakṣasyāpyapohaviṣayatvavyavasthā karttumucitā; tasya śābdapratyayasyeva vastuviṣayatve vivādābhāvāt / vidhiśabdena ca yathādhyavasāyamatadrūpa parāvṛtto bāhyorthobhimataḥ / yathāpratibhāsaṃ buḍdhyākāraśca; tatra vāhyorthodhyavasāyādeva śabdavācyo vyavasthāpyate / na svalakṣaṇaparisphūrttyā pratyakṣavaddeśakālāvasthāniyatapravyakta svalakṣaṇāsphuraṇāt / yacchāstraṃ //
body.translated_text: Now, [the object] is excluded from others by the force of its universal (<s>jāti</s>). Let it be excluded from others by the force of the universal or by the force of the continuity of its own causal series — in either case, in the cognition of what is excluded, the cognition of exclusion indeed exists. Nor is there the defect of mutual dependence (<s>anyonyāśraya</s>) in establishing the convention of the word 'cow' for what is excluded from non-cow. Even in establishing the convention for the universal or for what possesses it, there is scope for that very defect. For what is meant by 'universal' is not mere universality — otherwise, the word 'cow' would apply to a horse as well — but rather 'cowness' (<s>gotva</s>). And with that, the very same defect [arises]: since without knowing cows, the universal 'cowness' is not known; and without knowing the universal 'cowness,' what is denoted by the word 'cow' is not known. Therefore, the conceptual mental image (<s>vikalpabuddhyākāra</s>) that arises after seeing even a single individual — as if externally imposed and common to all instances — it is upon that image that the convention 'this is a cow' is established, without the defect of mutual dependence. And when the application of the word 'cow' is accepted [for certain objects], it is fitting that the remainder is also denoted by the word 'non-cow.' Nor is there any contradiction between exclusion-from-others (<s>anyāpoḍha</s>) and exclusion (<s>anyāpoha</s>), nor any damage to the qualifier-qualified relation — because there is no mutual exclusion between them, and co-reference (<s>sāmānādhikaraṇya</s>) does exist, just as with 'the pot [that is] on the ground' and 'the absence of the pot [elsewhere].' For contradiction is through one's own nature, not through the absence of another — this is well-known even to a child. In the [statement] 'this path leads to <s>Śrughna</s>,' exclusion is indeed understood — 'this one alone' in relation to other irrelevant paths; 'to <s>Śrughna</s> alone' in relation to undesirable places opposed to <s>Śrughna</s>; '[it] indeed leads' by the absence of interruption as with a forest path; '[it is] a path' by the exclusion of caravans, messengers, and the like — since exclusion is easily obtainable at every word. Therefore, from words, there is cognition of the positive content (<s>vidhirūpa</s>) that has the property of exclusion — just as from the word '<s>puṇḍarīka</s>' (white lotus), [one cognizes] a lotus qualified by whiteness. If so, it would be appropriate to say that positive content alone is the meaning of a word — why then is <s>apoha</s> (exclusion) spoken of? The answer has been given: by the word <s>apoha</s>, positive content qualified by exclusion-from-others is meant. When positive content is cognized, exclusion-from-others is simultaneously cognized as its qualifier. Nor is it appropriate to establish that direct perception too has exclusion as its object, since there is no dispute about its having a real object, unlike conceptual cognition from words. By the term 'positive content,' the external object — turned away from what is not of that nature — is meant as determined by conceptual judgment (<s>adhyavasāya</s>). And the mental image [is meant] as it appears. The external object, precisely through conceptual determination, is established as the referent of the word — not through the manifestation of the <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> (particular) as in direct perception, because the <s>svalakṣaṇa</s>, restricted to specific place, time, and condition, does not manifest [in verbal cognition]. As the treatise states:

body.text: śabdenāvyāpṛtākhyasya buddhvāvapratibhāsanāt /
body.translated_text: Because what is not denoted by a word does not appear in cognition —

body.text: arthasya dṛṣṭāviveti, indriyaśabdasvabhāvopāyabhedāt ekasyaiva pratibhāsa bheda iti cet? atrāpyuktam /
body.translated_text: [the object] is as if seen. If it be said that the difference in appearance of one and the same thing is due to the difference in means — sense-faculty, word, and inherent nature — to this too it has been said:

children.translated_text: When the basis called 'name' is different from the internal object,
how can a single thing have a form that appears in different aspects?

body.text: na hi spaṣṭāspaṣṭe dve rūpe parasparaviruḍdhe ekasya vastunaḥ staḥ; yata ekenendriyabuḍdhau pratibhāsetānyena vikalpe, tathā sati vastuna eva bhedaprāpteḥ; na hi svarūpabhedādaparo vastubhedaḥ / na ca pratibhāsabhedādapara svarūpabhedaḥ; anyathā trailokyamekameva vastu syāt / dūrāsannadeśavarttinoḥ puruṣayoḥ ekatra śākhini spaṣṭāspaṣṭapratibhāsabhedepi na śākhibheda iti cet? na brūmaḥ pratibhāsabhedobhinnavastu niyataḥ / kintu , ekaviṣayatvābhāvaniyata iti / tato yatrārthakriyābhedādisacivaḥ pratibhāsabhedaḥ tatra vastubhedaḥ, ghaṭavat / anyatra punarnniyame naikaviṣayatāṃ pariharatītyekapratibhāso bhrāntaḥ /
body.translated_text: For a single object does not have two mutually contradictory forms — one clear and one unclear — such that by one it appears in sense-cognition and by the other in conceptual thought. If that were so, the object itself would be divided; for there is no division of the object apart from the division of its own nature. Nor is there a division of own-nature apart from the division of appearance — otherwise, the three worlds would be a single object. If it be objected: 'For two persons situated near and far, even though there is a difference of clear and unclear appearance regarding a single tree, there is no difference in the tree' — [we reply:] We do not say that difference in appearance necessarily entails different objects. Rather, it necessarily entails the absence of having a single object. Therefore, where the difference in appearance is accompanied by a difference in causal efficacy (<s>arthakriyā</s>) and the like, there is a difference in objects, as with pots. In other cases, however, the restriction does not remove the single-objectness — [rather,] one of the appearances is erroneous.

body.text: etena yadāha vācaspatiḥ; na ca śabdapratyakṣayovvastugocaratve pratyayābhedaḥ kāraṇabhedena pārokṣyāpārokṣyabhedopapatteriti / tannopayogi / parokṣapratyayasya vastugocaratvāsamarthanāt / parokṣatāśrayastu kāraṇabheda indriyagocaragrahaṇaviraheṇaiva kṛtārthaḥ / tanna śābde pratyaye svalakṣaṇam parisphurati kiñca svalakṣaṇātmani vastuni vācye sarvvātmanā pratipatteḥ, vidhiniṣedhayorayogaḥ / tasya hi sadbhāvestīti vyartha, nāstītyasamartham; asadbhāve nāstīti vyarthamastī tyasamartham / asti cāstyādipadaprayogaḥ / tasmāt śabdapratibhāsasya vāhyārthabhāvābhāvasādhāraṇyaṃ na tadviṣayatāṃ kṣamate /
body.translated_text: By this, what <s>Vācaspati</s> [Miśra] states — namely, 'There is no difference of cognition when both verbal and perceptual [cognitions] have a real object as their domain, since the difference of directness and indirectness is explicable by the difference of cause' — that is not useful, because the real-object-domain character of indirect cognition is not established. The difference of cause that underlies indirectness is already fulfilled by the mere absence of apprehension through a sense faculty. Therefore, the particular (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>) does not shine forth in verbal cognition. Moreover, if the real thing with its nature as a particular were what is denoted, then affirmation and negation would be impossible. For regarding what exists, 'it exists' is redundant and 'it does not exist' is incapable [of being true]; regarding what does not exist, 'it does not exist' is redundant and 'it exists' is incapable. And yet there is the use of words like 'exists' and so forth. Therefore, the object appearing in verbal cognition, being common to both the existence and non-existence of the external object, does not tolerate being the domain of that [real particular].

body.text: yacca vācaspatinā jātimabdyaktivācyatāṃ svavācaiva prastu tyānanantarameva na ca śabdārthasya jāterbhāvābhāvasādhāraṇyaṃ nopapadyate; sā hi svarūpato nityāpi deśakālaviprakīrṇānekavyaktyāśrayatayā bhāvābhāvasādhāraṇībhavannastinā stisambandhayogyā; varttamānavyaktisambandhitā hi jāterastitā; atītānāgatavyaktisambandhitā ca nāstiteti sandigdhavyatirekitvādanaikāntikambhāvābhāvasādhāraṇyamanyathāsiḍvaṃ veti vilapitaṃ / tāvanna prakṛtakṣatiḥ / jātau bharaṃ nyasyatā svalakṣaṇāvācyatvasya svayaṃ svīkārāt / kiñca sarvvatra padārthasya svalakṣaṇasvarūpeṇaivāstitvādikaṃ cintyate / jātestu varttamānādivyaktisambandho stitvādikamiti tu bālapratāraṇam / evaṃ jātimavdhyaktivacane 'pi doṣaḥ; vyakteścet pratītisiddhiḥ, jātiradhikā pratīyatām, mā vā, na tu vyaktipratītidoṣanmuktiḥ / ete na yaducyate kaumārilaiḥ / sabhāgatvādeva vastuno na sādhāraṇyadoṣaḥ / vṛkṣatvaṃ hyanirdvāritabhāvābhāvaṃ śabdādavagamyate / tayoranyatareṇa śabdāntarāvagatena sambadhyata iti / tadapyasaṅgatam; sāmānyasya nityasya pratipattāvanirdvāritabhāvābhāvatvāyogāt / yacceḍhaṃ na ca pratyakṣasyeva śabdānāṃ arthapratyāyanaprakāro yena taddṛṣṭa ivāstyādiśabdāpekṣā na syāt; vicitraśaktitvāt pramāṇānāmiti tadapyaindriyakaśābdapratibhāsayorekasvarūpagrāhitve bhinnāvabhāsadūṣaṇena dūṣitam vicitraśaktitvañca pramāṇānāṃ sākṣātkārādhyavasāyābhyāmapi caritārtham /
body.translated_text: And as for what <s>Vācaspati</s> babbles — having himself introduced the universal (<s>jāti</s>) as what is denotable by words, and then immediately [saying], 'Nor is it untenable that the universal, the word's referent, should be common to existence and non-existence; for though it is eternal in its own nature, by being the substratum of many particulars (<s>vyakti</s>) scattered across space and time, it becomes common to existence and non-existence, and is fit for relation with both "exists" and "does not exist." For the existence of the universal is its relation with present particulars; and its non-existence is its relation with past and future particulars. Therefore, the commonality of existence and non-existence is an inconclusive [reason] with doubtful negative concomitance (<s>sandigdhavyatirekin</s>), or else is established otherwise.' First, there is no damage to the main thesis, since one who places the burden on the universal has himself accepted the non-denotability of the particular (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>). Furthermore, the existence and so forth of a word's referent is conceived everywhere only in terms of its own nature as a particular. But the claim that the universal's existence-and-so-forth consists in its relation with present and other particulars is a deception of the naive. Likewise, there is the same fault even if the universal is said to denote [through] the particular: if the particular is established through cognition, let the universal additionally be cognized or not — but there is no escape from the fault of cognizing a particular [directly through words]. Now, as to what the <s>Kumārila</s> followers say — namely, 'There is no defect of commonality for the real object, precisely because of [its] homogeneous nature (<s>sabhāgatva</s>); for tree-ness is apprehended from the word as having undetermined existence or non-existence, and is then connected with one or the other [existence or non-existence] that is known through another word' — that too is incoherent, because the universal, being eternal, cannot have undetermined existence and non-existence as what is cognized. And as for the assertion, 'The mode of conveying objects by words is not like that of perception, so that — as in the case of perception — there would be no need for words like "exists" and so on, because the means of knowledge have varied powers' — that too has been refuted by the objection that if the content of sensory and verbal appearances has a single nature, there would be the fault of distinct appearances. And the varied powers of the means of knowledge are already accounted for by direct experience (<s>sākṣātkāra</s>) and determination (<s>adhyavasāya</s>).

body.text: tato yadi pratyakṣārthapratipādanaṃ śābdena tadvadevāvabhāsaḥ syāt; abhavaṃśca na tadviṣayakhyāpanaṃ kṣamate / nanu vṛkṣaśabdena vṛkṣatvāṃśe codite sattvādyaṃśaniścayanārthamastyādipadaprayoga iti cet? niraṃśatvena pratyakṣasamadhigatasya svalakṣaṇasya ko 'vakāśaḥ padāntareṇa; dharmmāntaravidhiniṣedhayoḥ pramāṇāntareṇa vā / pratyakṣe 'pi pramāṇāntarāpekṣā dṛṣṭe ti cet? bhavatu tasyāniścayātmatvāt anabhyastasvarūpaviṣaye; vikalpastu svayanniścayātmako yatra grāhī tatra kimapareṇa? asti ca śabdaliṅgāntarāpekṣā tato na vastu svarūpagrahaḥ / nanu bhinnā jātyādayo dharmmāḥ parasparaṃ dharmmiṇaśceti jātilakṣaṇaikadharmmadvāreṇa pratītepi śākhini dharmmāntaravattayā na pratītiriti kinna bhinnā bhidhānādhī no dharmāntarasya nīlacaloccaistaratvāderavavodhaḥ / tadetadasaṅgatam; akhaṇḍātmanaḥ svalakṣaṇasya pratyakṣe pratibhāsāt / dṛśyasya dharmmadharmmibhedasya pratyakṣapratikṣiptatvā danyathā sarvvaṃ sarvvatra syādityatiprasaṅgaḥ / kālpanikabhedāśrayastu dharmmadharmmivyavahāra iti prasādhitam śāstre; bhavatu vā paramārthiko dharmmadharmmibhedaḥ / tathāpyanayoḥ samavāyāde rdūṣitatvādupakāralakṣaṇaiva pratyāsattireṣitavyā / evañca yathendriyapratyāsattyā pratyakṣeṇa dharmmipratipattau sakalataddvarmmapratipattiḥ / tathā śabdaliṅgābhyāmapi vācyavācakādi sambandhapratibaddhābhyāṃ dharmmipratipattau niravaśeṣataḍvarmmapratipatti rbhavet; pratyāsattimātrasyāviśeṣāt /
body.translated_text: Therefore, if verbal [cognition] were to present the object of perception, it would have to appear in exactly the same way; and non-existence would be unable to make known the object of that [perception]. Now, if it is objected: 'When the word "vṛkṣa" (tree) evokes the tree-aspect, words like "asti" (exists) are employed for the purpose of determining other aspects such as existence (<s>sattva</s>)' — [we reply:] since the <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> (particular) as apprehended by perception is partless, what scope is there for an additional word, or for another means of proof, in enjoining or prohibiting a different property? If it is objected: 'Even in perception there is dependence on another means of proof, as is observed' — let it be so, since [perception] is of the nature of non-determination regarding an object whose form has not been habitually encountered. But conceptual cognition (<s>vikalpa</s>) is itself of the nature of determination — where it grasps, what need is there of another? And there is indeed dependence on other words and inferential marks (<s>liṅga</s>); therefore there is no grasping of the real nature of an object [through words alone]. Now, if it is objected: 'The properties such as universal (<s>jāti</s>) etc. are distinct from each other and from the property-possessor (<s>dharmin</s>), and so even when a tree is cognized through the single property of universal-characterization, it is not cognized as possessing other properties — so why should not distinct verbal cognitions fail to convey other properties such as blue, moving, tall, etc.?' — this is incoherent, because the <s>svalakṣaṇa</s>, whose nature is undivided, appears in perception [as a whole]. Since the difference between property (<s>dharma</s>) and property-possessor (<s>dharmin</s>), which is [supposedly] perceived, is in fact rejected by perception, otherwise there would be the absurd consequence that everything would be [perceived] everywhere. However, the conventional usage of property and property-possessor resting on a merely constructed distinction has been established in the [Buddhist] treatises. Or let there be a real distinction between property and property-possessor — even so, since [connecting relations like] <s>samavāya</s> (inherence) etc. between these two have been refuted, only proximity characterized by causal efficacy (<s>upakāra</s>) should be accepted. And thus, just as in perception, when the property-possessor is apprehended through the proximity of the sense-faculty, all its properties are apprehended; so also through words and inferential marks, which are bound by the relation of signifier and signified, when the property-possessor is apprehended, there should be apprehension of all its properties without exception — since there is no difference in proximity as such.

body.text: yacca vācaspatiḥ; nacaikopādhinā sattve viśiṣṭe tasmin gṛhīte; upādhyanta raviśiṣṭatabgdrahaḥ / svabhāvoṃ hi dravyasya upādhibhirvviśiṣyate / natūpādhayo vā viśeṣyatvaṃ vā tasya svabhāva iti / tadapi plavata eva / nahyabhedādupādhyantaragrahaṇañcamāsañji tam / bhedaṃ puraskṛtyaivopakārakagrahaṇe upakāryyagrahaṇaprasañjanāt / na cāgnidhūmayoḥ kāryyakāraṇabhāva iva svabhāvata eva dharmmadharmmiṇoḥ pratiniyamakalpanamucitam / tayorapi pramāṇāsiddha tvāt / pramāṇasiddhe ca svabhāvopavarṇanamiti nyāyaḥ //
body.translated_text: And as for what <s>Vācaspati</s> [Miśra] says: 'When an entity qualified by one <s>upādhi</s> (limiting condition) is grasped, there is no grasping of it as qualified by another <s>upādhi</s>; for the nature of a substance is qualified by its <s>upādhis</s>, but the <s>upādhis</s> themselves and the state of being qualified are not its [intrinsic] nature' — this too is groundless. For, given non-difference [between substance and its properties], the grasping of another <s>upādhi</s> cannot be avoided. And if one proceeds on the basis of difference, then grasping the helper would entail grasping the helped. Nor is it proper to posit a fixed natural connection between property and property-possessor, as between fire and smoke in a cause-effect relation — for even that [relation] is not established by a means of proof. And the principle is: one describes the [intrinsic] nature only of what is established by a means of proof.

body.text: yaccātra nyāyabhūṣaṇena sūryyādigrahaṇe tadupakāryyāśeṣa vasturāśigrahaṇaprasañjanamuktam; tadabhiprāyānavagāhana phalam tathā hi tvanmate dharmmadharmmiṇorbhedaḥ upakāralakṣaṇaiva ca pratyāsattiḥ / tadopakārakagrahaṇe samānadeśasyaiva dharmmarūpasyaiva copakāryyasya grahaṇamāsañjitam / tat kathaṃ sūryyo pakāryyasya bhinnadeśasya dravyāntarasya vā dṛṣṭavyabhicārasya grahaṇaprasaṅgaḥ saṅgataḥ / tasmāt ekadharmmadvāreṇāpi vastusvarūpapratipattau sarvvātmapratīteḥ; kva śabdāntareṇa vidhiniṣedhāvakāśaḥ / asti ca, tasmānna svalakṣaṇasya śabdavikalpaliṅgapratibhāsitvamiti sthitam //
body.translated_text: And as for what is said here by the author of the <s>Nyāyabhūṣaṇa</s> — that grasping the sun would entail grasping the entire aggregate of objects benefited by it — that is the result of not penetrating the intended meaning. For in your view, there is a difference between property and property-possessor, and proximity is characterized by causal efficacy alone. In that case, when the helper is grasped, it is only the property that is co-located [with it] and that is itself the helped that should be grasped — this much [alone] is entailed. Then how is the absurd consequence of grasping an object benefited by the sun, which is in a different location and is a different substance, and for which deviation [from the rule] is observed, at all coherent? Therefore, since even through a single property-door the apprehension of the real nature of the object entails cognition of its entire self, where is there scope for enjoining or prohibiting through an additional word? And yet there is [such scope] — therefore it is established that <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> (the particular) does not appear in verbal cognition, conceptual cognition, or inferential marks.

body.text: nāpi sāmānyam śābdapratyayapratibhāsi / saritaḥ pāre gāvaścarantīti gavādiśabdāt sāsrāśṛṅgalāṅgūlādayo 'kṣarākāraparikaritāḥ sajātīyabhedāparāmarśanāt sampiṇḍitaprāyāḥ pratibhāsante / na ca tadeva sāmānyam /
body.translated_text: Nor is it the universal (<s>sāmānya</s>) that appears in verbal cognition. [For when one hears] 'Cows are grazing on the far bank of the river,' from words like 'go' (cow) etc., what appear are [forms] furnished with horns, tails, etc. in letter-like configurations, roughly aggregated due to the non-apprehension of differences among members of the same class. But that is not itself the universal.

body.text: varṇākṛtyakṣarākāraśrūnyaṅgotvaṃ hi kathyate /
body.translated_text: For <s>gotva</s> (cowness) is described as devoid of color, shape, letter-form, and bodily parts.

body.text: tadeva ca sāsrāśṛṅgādimātramakhilavyaktāvatyantavilakṣaṇamapi svalakṣaṇenaikīkriyamāṇam sāmānyamityucyate / tādṛśasya vāhyasyāprāpte rbhrāntirevāsau keśapratibhāsavat / tasmādvāsanāvaśādduḍvereva tadātmanā vivarttoyamastu, asadeva vā tadrūpaṃ khyātu; vyaktaya eva vā sajātīyabhedatiraskāreṇānyathā bhāsantā manubhavavyavadhānāt; smṛtipramoṣo vabhidhīyatām; sarvvathā nirvviṣayaḥ khalvayaṃ sāmānyapratyayaḥ; kva sāmānyavārttā? yat punaḥ sāmānyābhāve sāmānyapratyayasyākasmikatvamuktaṃ tadayuktam / yataḥ pūrvvapiṇḍadaṇḍadarśanasmaraṇasahakāriṇātiricyamānāviśeṣapratyayajanikā sāmagrī nirvviṣayaṃ sāmānyavikalpamutpādayati / tadevanna śābdapratyaye jātiḥ pratibhāti; nāpi pratyakṣe na cānumānato 'pi siddhiḥ; adṛśyatve pratibaddhaliṅgādarśanāt / nāpīndriyavadasyāḥ siddhiḥ / jñānakāryyataḥ kādācitkasyaiva nimittāntarasya siddheḥ / yadāpi piṇḍāntare antarāle vā gobuddherabhāvaṃ darśayet; tadā śāvaleyādisakalagopiṇḍānāmevābhāvādabhāvo go buddherūpapadyamānaḥ kathamarthāntaramākṣipet? gotvādeva gopiṇḍaḥ, anyathā turagopi gopiṇḍaḥ syāt / yadyevaṃ gopiṇḍādeva gotvamanyathā turagatvamapi gotvam syāt / tasmāt kāraṇaparamparāta eva gopiṇḍo gotvaṃ tu bhavatu mā vā / nanu sāmānyapratyayajananasāmarthyaṃ yadyekasmāt piṇḍādabhinnam; tadā vijātīyavyāvṛttaṃ piṇḍāntaramasamarthaṃ / atha bhinnaṃ tadā tadeva sāmānyam nāmni paraṃ vivāda iti cet? abhinnaiva sā śaktiḥ prati vastu; yathātvekaḥ śaktasvabhāvo bhāvaḥ tatha anyopi bhavan kīdṛśandoṣamāvahati? yathā bhavatāṃ jātirekāpi samānadhvaniprasavaheturanyāpi svarūpeṇaiva jātyantaranirapekṣā / tathāsmākaṃ vyaktirapi jātinirapekṣā svarūpeṇaiva bhinnā hetuḥ /
body.translated_text: And that very thing — which is merely [something with] dewlap, horns, and so forth, entirely different from all particulars — being unified by its own particular nature, is called 'universal' (<s>sāmānya</s>). Since such an external [entity] is not attained, this is mere illusion, like the appearance of hairs [to one with an eye disease]. Therefore, let this be a transformation (<s>vivarta</s>) of the cognition itself, under the force of latent impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>), in that form; or let that which is unreal appear in that form; or let the particulars (<s>vyakti</s>) themselves appear otherwise by concealing the differences among those of the same class, due to the interruption of [continuous] experience; or let it be called loss of memory. In all cases, this universal-cognition is indeed objectless — where is there any talk of a universal? The further objection that in the absence of universals, universal-cognition would be causeless — that is unfounded. For the aggregate of causes, aided by the memory of prior observation of individual things and sticks, generating a cognition in which no distinction is apprehended, produces an objectless universal-concept (<s>sāmānyavikalpa</s>). Thus the universal (<s>jāti</s>) does not appear in verbal cognition; nor in perception; nor is it established by inference either — because, if it is invisible, the inferential mark bound to it is not observed. Nor is its establishment analogous to that of the sense organs, since from the effect of cognition only an occasional other cause is established. Even when one shows the absence of cow-cognition in another individual or in the interval, since the absence of cow-cognition is explained by the very absence of all cow-individuals such as <s>Śāvaleya</s> and the rest, how could it indicate a separate entity? [Objection:] It is from cowness (<s>gotva</s>) alone that a cow-individual [is a cow-individual]; otherwise, a horse too would be a cow-individual. [Reply:] If so, then cowness itself [comes] from the cow-individual; otherwise, horse-ness too would be cowness. Therefore, the cow-individual [arises] from a causal chain alone; as for cowness — it may or may not exist. [Objection:] But if the capacity to generate universal-cognition is non-different from one individual, then another individual differentiated from heterogeneous kinds would be incapable [of generating it]. If [it is] different, then that itself is the universal — the dispute is merely about the name, is it? [Reply:] That capacity is indeed non-different in each individual thing. Just as one entity has the nature of being capable, so too another — what fault does this bring? Just as for you, one universal is the cause of producing the same word, while another universal too, by its own nature alone, is independent of other universals; so too for us, each particular (<s>vyakti</s>), independent of universals, by its own nature alone, is a distinct cause.

body.text: yattu trilocanaḥ / aśvatvagotvā dīnāṃ sāmānya viśeṣāṇāṃ svāśraye samavāyaḥ sāmānyam; sāmānya mityabhidhānapratyayayornimittamiti / yadyevaṃ vyaktiṣvapyayameva tathābhidhānapratyayaheturastu / kiṃ sāmānyasvīkāra pramādena /
body.translated_text: As for what <s>Trilocana</s> [states]: 'The inherence (<s>samavāya</s>) of universals and particulars such as horse-ness, cow-ness, etc., in their own substrata is the "universal" and is the cause of the designation and cognition called "universal"' — if so, let this very same thing in the particulars themselves be the cause of such designation and cognition. What is the point of the error of accepting a universal?

body.text: na ca samavāyaḥ sambhavī //
body.translated_text: And inherence (<s>samavāya</s>) is not possible.

children.text: iheti buddheḥ samavāyasiddhiriheti dhīśca dvayadarśane syāt /
children.translated_text: The establishment of inherence depends on the cognition 'here [it inheres],' and the cognition 'here' would arise only upon the observation of both [relata].
But there is no dependence on its object anywhere; therefore [inherence] is merely one's own fabrication.

body.text: etena yeyaṃ pratyayānuvṛttiranuvṛttavastvanuyāyinī kathamatyantabhedinīsu vyaktiṣu vyāvṛttaviṣayapratyayabhāvānupātinīṣu bhavitumarhatītyuhāpravarttanamasya pratyākhyātam / jāṭiṣveva parasparavyāvṛttatayā vyaktīyamānāsvanuvṛttapratyayena vyabhicārāt / yat punaranena viparyyaye vādhakamuktam, abhidhānapratyayānuvṛttiḥ kutaścinnivṛttya kvacideva bhavantī nimittavatī / na cānyannimittamityādi // tanna samyak / anuvṛttamantareṇāpi abhidhānapratyayānuvṛtteratadrūpaparāvṛttasvarūpaviśeṣāt avaśyaṃ svīkārasya sādhitatvāt / tasmāt, tulya bhede yayā jā tiḥ pratyāsattyā prasarpati / kvacinnānyatra saivāstu śabdajñānanibandhanam /
body.translated_text: By this, the [objection that] this recurrence of cognition follows a recurrent object — [asking] how can it obtain in particulars that are absolutely different, in which the cognitions follow objects that are [each] differentiated — this speculation is refuted. For in universals themselves, being manifest as mutually differentiated, there would be deviation from recurrent cognition. As for the counter-proof he stated for the converse — 'the recurrence of designation and cognition, ceasing from certain things and occurring in certain things alone, has a cause, and there is no other cause,' etc. — that is not correct. Because even without a [real] recurrent entity, the recurrence of designation and cognition must be accepted, due to the particular nature [of each individual] that is excluded from what is not of that form. Therefore, in what is equally differentiated, the proximity by which the universal extends in certain instances and not in others — let that very [proximity] be the ground of verbal cognition.

body.text: yat punaratra nyāyabhūṣaṇenoktaṃ nahyevaṃ bhavati / yayā pratyāsattyā daṇḍasūtrādikaṃ prasarpati kvacinnānyatra saiva pratyāsattiḥ puruṣasphaṭikādiṣu daṇḍisūtritvādivyavahāranibandhanamastu kiṃ daṇḍasūtrādineti / tadasaṅgatam / daṇḍasūtrayohi puruṣasphaṭikapratyāsannayoḥ dṛṣṭayoḥ daṇḍisūtripratyayahetutvaṃ nāpalapyate / sāmānyantu svapne 'pi na dṛṣṭam / tadyadīdaṃ parikalpanīyam tadā varam pratyāsattireva sāmānyapratyayahetuḥ parikalpyatām, kiṃ gurvyāparikalpanayetyabhiprāyā parijñānāt /
body.translated_text: Furthermore, as for what was said here by [the author of] the <s>Nyāyabhūṣaṇa</s> — 'it is not so; the very proximity by which [the cognition] 'staff-bearer,' 'thread-bearer,' and the like spreads to some things and not to others, let that very proximity be the ground of the conventional usage 'staff-bearer,' 'thread-bearer,' etc., with respect to a man, crystal, and so forth — what need is there of [a universal residing in] the staff, thread, and the like?' — that is incoherent. For the staff and thread, which are seen as proximate to the man and the crystal, are not denied to be the cause of the cognitions 'staff-bearer' and 'thread-bearer.' But the universal is never seen, not even in a dream. So if this [universal] is to be hypothesized, it is better that proximity itself be hypothesized as the cause of the cognition of a universal — what need is there for the heavier hypothesis [of the universal]? — since [the opponent's true] intention is thereby fully understood.

body.text: athedaṃ jātiprasādhakamanumānamabhidhīyate /
body.translated_text: Now, this inference is stated as establishing the universal (<s>jāti</s>):

body.text: yadviśiṣṭajñānaṃ tadviśeṣaṇagrahaṇanāntarīyakam / yathā daṇḍijñānam / viśiṣṭajñānañcedaṃ gaurayamityarthataḥ kāryyahetuḥ / viśeṣaṇānubhavakāryyaṃ hi dṛṣṭānte viśiṣṭabuddhiḥ siḍveti / atrānuyogaḥ, viśiṣṭabuddherbhinnaviśeṣaṇagrahaṇanāntarīyakatvaṃ vā sādhyam; viśeṣaṇa mātrānubhavanāntarīyakatvaṃ vā / prathamapakṣe pakṣasya pratyakṣavādhāsādhanāvadhānamanavakāśayati / vastugrāhiṇaḥ pratyakṣasyo bhayapratibhāsābhāvāt / viśiṣṭabuddhitvañca sāmānyam / hetura naikāntikaḥ / bhinnaviśeṣaṇagrahaṇamantareṇāpi darśanāt / yathā svarūpavān ghaṭaḥ / gotvaṃ sāmānyamiti vā / dvitīyapakṣe tu siddhasādhanam / svarūpavān ghaṭa ityādivat gotvajātimā n piṇḍa iti parikalpitam bhedamupādāya viśeṣaṇaviśeṣyabhāvasyeṣṭatvādgovyāvṛttānubhavabhāvitvād gaurayamiti vyavahārasya / tadeva na sāmānyabuddhiḥ / vādhakaṃ ca sāmānyaguṇakarmmādyupā dhicakrasya, kevalavyaktigrāhakaṃ paṭupratyakṣam / dṛśyānupalambho vā prasiddhaḥ /
body.translated_text: A cognition of a qualified [thing] is invariably concomitant with the grasping of its qualifier. For example, the cognition 'staff-bearer.' And this cognition 'this is a cow' is a cognition of a qualified [thing] — so by implication it is an effect-reason (<s>kāryahetu</s>). For in the example, the cognition of the qualified [thing] is established as the effect of the experience of the qualifier. Here is the [critical] inquiry: is the thing to be proved that the cognition of the qualified [thing] is invariably concomitant with the grasping of a distinct qualifier, or that it is invariably concomitant with the mere experience of the qualifier? On the first alternative, the [proof] leaves no scope for warding off the demonstration that the thesis (<s>pakṣa</s>) is contradicted by perception (<s>pratyakṣabādhā</s>). For there is no dual appearance in perception, which grasps the real entity. And [the property of] being a cognition of a qualified [thing] is [itself] a universal; [so] the reason is inconclusive (<s>anaikāntika</s>), because [such cognition] is seen even without the grasping of a distinct qualifier — as in 'the pot possessing its own form,' or '[the universal] cowness is a universal.' On the second alternative, there is proving the already-established (<s>siddhasādhana</s>); for, just as in 'the pot possessing its own form' and the like, the qualifier-qualified relation [is accepted] with respect to 'the lump possessing the universal cowness,' adopting a constructed (<s>parikalpita</s>) difference, since the usage 'this is a cow' arises from the experience of [the object] as excluded from non-cow. And that very [cognition] is not a cognition of a universal. And there is a contradicting [proof]: against the whole array of limiting conditions (<s>upādhi</s>) — universal, quality, action, and so forth — there is keen perception (<s>paṭupratyakṣa</s>) grasping the bare individual, or else the well-known non-apprehension of what would [otherwise] be perceptible (<s>dṛśyānupalambha</s>).

body.text: tadevaṃ vidhireva śabdārthaḥ / sa ca vāhyortho budhyākāraśca vivakṣitaḥ, tatra na budhyākārasya tattvataḥ sambṛttyā vā vidhiniṣedhau / svasambedanapratyakṣagamyatvāt / anadhyavasāyācca / nāpi tattvato vāhyasyāpi vidhiniṣedhau tasya śābde pratyaye 'pratibhāsanāt / ataeva sarvvadharmmāṇāntattvato 'nabhilāpyatvaṃ pratibhāsādhyavasāyābhāvāt tasmāt vāhyasyaiva sāmbṛtau vidhiniṣedhau / anyathā samvyavahārahāniprasaṅgāt / tadevaṃ /
body.translated_text: Thus, the positive entity (<s>vidhi</s>) alone is the meaning of a word. And that is intended [in two ways]: as the external object (<s>bāhyārtha</s>) and as the form of cognition (<s>buddhyākāra</s>). Of these, there is no affirmation or negation (<s>vidhiniṣedha</s>) of the form of cognition, either ultimately or conventionally — because it is accessible to the perception of self-awareness (<s>svasaṃvedanapratyakṣa</s>), and because it is not [an object of] conceptual determination (<s>anadhyavasāya</s>). Nor, ultimately, are there affirmation and negation of the external [object] either, because it does not appear in verbal cognition. For this very reason, all <s>dharmas</s> are ultimately inexpressible (<s>anabhilāpya</s>), because there is no determination through appearance. Therefore, affirmation and negation belong to the external [object] alone, conventionally; otherwise there would follow the destruction of all ordinary discourse. Thus:

children.translated_text: Neither of the [cognitive] form nor of the external [object] is affirmation [established] ultimately;

children.text: vahireva hi saṃvṛttyā saṃvṛtyāpi tu nākṛteḥ //
children.translated_text: for [it is] only the external [object], conventionally — but even conventionally, not the [conceptual] image (<s>ākṛti</s>). //

body.text: etena yaḍvarmmottaraḥ // āropitasya vāhyatvasya vidhiniṣedhāvityalaukikamanāgamamatārkikīyaṃ kathayati / tadapahastitam /
body.translated_text: By this, the follower of [the doctrine that] the affirmation and negation are of a superimposed externality — namely, [the author of] the <s>Yuktidīpikā</s>(?) and his successor — proclaims something un-worldly, unscriptural, and unfit for a logician. That is [hereby] thrown out.

body.text: nanvadhyavasāye yadyadhyavaseyaṃ vastu na sphurati tadā tadadhyavasitamiti ko 'rthaḥ? apratibhāse 'pi pravṛttiviṣayīkṛtamiti yo 'rthaḥ / apratibhāsāviśeṣe viṣayāntaraparihāreṇa kathanniyataviṣayā pravṛttiriti cet? ucyate; yadyapi viśvamagṛhītaṃ tathāpi vikalpasya niyatasāmagrīprasūtatvena niyatākāratayā niyataśaktitvāt niyatā eva jalādau pravṛttiḥ / dhūmasya parokṣāgnijñānajananavat /
body.translated_text: Now [it may be objected]: in conceptual determination (<s>adhyavasāya</s>), if the thing to be determined does not flash forth, then what is the meaning of 'that has been determined'? [The answer is:] the meaning is that, even though it does not appear, it has been made the object of activity (<s>pravṛtti</s>). [Objection:] if there is no difference in [the fact of] non-appearance, how can activity be restricted to a determinate object by way of avoiding other objects? [The answer] is stated: although the whole [array of things] is not grasped, nevertheless, since the conceptual cognition (<s>vikalpa</s>), being produced by a determinate aggregate of causes, has a determinate form and hence a determinate capacity, the activity is restricted to water and the like — just as smoke [produces] the cognition of unseen fire.

body.text: niyataviṣayā hibhāvāḥ pramāṇapariniṣṭhitasvabhāvā na śaktisāṅkaryyaparyyanuyogabhājaḥ / tasmāt tadadhyavasāyitvamākāraviśeṣayogāt tatpravṛttijanakatvam / na ca sādṛśyādāropeṇa pravṛttiṃ brūmaḥ / yenākāre vāhyasya vāhye vā ākārasyāropadvāreṇa dūṣaṇāvakāśaḥ / kintarhi svavāsanāvipākavaśādupajāyamānaiva buḍvirapaśyantyapi vāhyaṃ vāhye vṛttimātano tīti viplutaiva / tadevamanyābhāvaviśiṣṭo vijātivyāvṛttortho vidhiḥ / sa eva cāpohaśabdavācyaḥ śabdānāmarthaḥ pravṛttinivṛttiviṣayaśceti sthitam //
body.translated_text: For entities have determinate objects, their natures being established by the means of valid cognition (<s>pramāṇa</s>); they are not liable to the objection of a confusion of capacities. Therefore, [the conceptual cognition's] being a determiner of that [object] is its being a producer of activity toward that, owing to its connection with a particular form. Nor do we say that activity occurs through superimposition based on similarity — whereby there would be scope for refutation by way of [arguing about] the superimposition of the external upon the [cognitive] form, or of the form upon the external. Rather, the cognition, arising merely through the maturation of its own latent dispositions (<s>vāsanā</s>), although not seeing the external [object], extends its operation upon the external [object] as if [seeing it] — being itself confused (<s>vipluta</s>). Thus it is established that the object qualified by the absence of others and excluded from the heterogeneous (<s>vijātivyāvṛtta</s>) is the positive entity (<s>vidhi</s>); and that very [positive entity] is what is denoted by the word <s>apoha</s>, is the meaning of words, and is the object of [their] application and exclusion. //

body.text: atra prayogaḥ / yadvācakaṃ tatsarvvamadhyavasitātadrūpaparāvṛttavastumātragocaram / yatheha kūpe jalamiti vacanam / vācakañcedaṃ gavādiśabdarūpamiti svabhāvahetuḥ / nāyamasiḍvaḥ, pūrvoktena nyāyena pāramārthikavācyavācakabhāvasyābhāve 'pi; adhyavasāyakṛtasya sarvvavyavahāribhiravaśyasvīkarttavyatvāt / anyathā sarvvavyavahārocchedaprasaṅgāt / nāpi viruddhaḥ sapakṣe bhāvāt / na cānaikāntikaḥ; tathāhi śabdānāmadhyavasitavijātivyāvṛttava stumātraviṣayatvamanicchadbhiḥ paraiḥ paramārthato
body.translated_text: Here is the formal argument: Whatever is a designator, all of that has as its scope only an entity that is turned away from what is not of that nature as determined by conceptual judgment. For example, the statement 'there is water in this well.' And this, having the form of the word 'cow' and the like, is a designator — this is the natural-property reason (<s>svabhāvahetu</s>). This [reason] is not unestablished (<s>asiddha</s>), because even in the absence of a real designator-designated relationship, as explained above, [the relationship] created by conceptual judgment must be accepted by all who engage in ordinary discourse — otherwise, all ordinary discourse would be destroyed. Nor is it contradicted (<s>viruddha</s>), since it is present in the similar case (<s>sapakṣa</s>). Nor is it inconclusive (<s>anaikāntika</s>). For opponents who do not accept that words have as their scope only an entity determined by exclusion from what is dissimilar, [must accept that] in ultimate reality

body.text: vācyaṃ svalakṣaṇamupādhirupādhiyogaḥ
body.translated_text: the designated is the <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> (particular), or a limiting condition (<s>upādhi</s>), or the connection with a limiting condition,

body.text: sopādhirastu yadi vā kṛtirastu buddheḥ, gatyantarābhāvāt / aviṣayatve ca vācakatvāyogāt / tatra /
body.translated_text: or what is qualified by the limiting condition, or alternatively a construction of the intellect — since there is no other possibility. And if [the particular] is not the object, designation would be impossible. Regarding this:

body.text: ādyantayornna samayaḥ phalaśaktihānermadhyepyupādhivirahāttitayena yuktaḥ //
body.translated_text: For the first and last [alternatives], the convention does not hold due to the loss of [causal] efficacy and power; for the middle one too, due to the absence of a limiting condition, [the convention] is established by the third [alternative].

body.text: tadevaṃ vācyāntarasyābhāvāt / viṣayavattvalakṣaṇasya vyāpakasya nivṛttau vipakṣato nivarttamānam vācakatvamadhyavasitavāhyaviṣayatvena vyāpyata iti vyāptisiddhiḥ /
body.translated_text: Thus, since there is no other possible designated [object], when the pervader — defined as having-an-object — is negated, the property of being a designator — which withdraws from the dissimilar case — is pervaded by having as its object the external entity as determined by conceptual judgment. Thus the pervasion (<s>vyāpti</s>) is established.

children.translated_text: By words, the object is primarily denoted; therein, <s>apoha</s> (exclusion) is understood as its attribute.

children.text: arthaścaiko 'dhyāsato bhāsato 'nyaḥ sthāpyo vācyastattvato naiva kaścit //
children.translated_text: The object is one through superimposition, but appears as another. The designated is to be established; in ultimate reality, nothing whatsoever [is designated].

body.text: apohasiddhiḥ samāptā //
body.translated_text: The <s>Apohasiddhi</s> (Establishment of Exclusion) is complete.

body.text: kṛtiriyammahāpaṇḍitaratnakīrttipādānām //
body.translated_text: This is the composition of the feet of the great <s>Paṇḍita</s> <s>Ratnakīrti</s>.

children.translated_text: Let the learned elaborate on <s>apoha</s>; the essential point, however, is the non-manifestation of the real nature of things.

children.text: tatrādṛḍhe sarvvamayatnaśīrṇaṃ dṛḍhe tu sausthyannanu tāvataiva //
children.translated_text: When that [point] is not firmly grasped, everything crumbles effortlessly; but when firmly grasped, well-being [arises] from that alone.
In two full watches of the night, the <s>Apoha</s> [treatise] of <s>Kīrti</s> (<s>Ratnakīrti</s>) was written with ease.
By <s>Trailokyadatta</s>, for the sake of others and oneself — therefore, this should be carefully preserved.
